# AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai -- registering this mod's two government types.
#
# GENERATED BY ln-audit-tools/gen_ln_defines.py. DO NOT HAND-EDIT. Re-run it after EVERY AGOT update.
#
# ==============================================================================================================
# THE LIST BELOW IS AGOT'S, COPIED VERBATIM, PLUS TWO LINES. IT IS NOT OURS TO CURATE.
# ==============================================================================================================
#
# WHY. common/defines merges at the KEY level -- so this file touches nothing but NGovernment.GOVERNMENT_TYPES,
# and every other define AGOT and Paradox set is untouched. But the VALUE of that one key is REPLACED wholesale,
# not appended to, so the full list has to be restated. If AGOT adds a government and this file is not
# regenerated, THEIR new one silently loses its opinion modifiers exactly the way ours were losing theirs.
#
# THAT ALREADY HAPPENED ONCE. AGOT 5.0 added lorathi_principality_government and norvos_government. This file
# was hand-maintained at the time and did not follow, so anyone running our mod on 5.0+ got a wall of
# "Could not find the preregistered modifier type" for both of them. Spotted and reported by AlbionPCJ on
# Discord; confirmed as a 5.0 addition by HadesOria. That is the whole reason the generator now exists.
#
# WHAT IT FIXES ON OUR SIDE. Twenty lines of setup.log:
#
#   Could not find the preregistered modifier type 'ln_ranger_government_opinion' [...] Are you sure the
#   government type 'ln_ranger_government' is included in the define GOVERNMENT_TYPES?
#
# Twelve for ln_ranger_government, eight for wight_government. Without registration the engine never creates
# a government's opinion, vassal_opinion, tributary_opinion, same-faith opinion, or its four contribution
# modifier pairs -- so vassal contracts and government-to-government opinion for both were running on nothing.
#
# ON OLD AGOT VERSIONS. A name listed here whose government is not defined costs nothing but an unused
# preregistered modifier -- there is no script that can run against it, and defines have no conditional
# syntax to guard with even if we wanted one. The asymmetry is the point: OMITTING a name that does exist
# breaks that government's modifiers outright, which is the bug we are fixing. Listing one that does not
# exist yet is inert. So the list stays a superset, and an AGOT 4.40 save keeps working.
